gen-dafont-stentiga-gf-kedebideri: Spaced-out and softly luxurious, Stentiga draws its letters with a line that keeps one width all the way around. Kedebideri follows in sans-serif form, rounded and approachable, with a skyward x-height that stays open.
gen-dafont-stentiga-gf-khula: Stentiga spreads its letters wide and lets every stroke keep its width. Khula, the sans-serif below, is the workhorse here, with a tall midsection and curves that hold their mouths open while the heading handles the show.
gen-dafont-stentiga-gf-krub: Refined and a little luxurious, Stentiga has round bowls whose walls never swell or taper. Krub brings a pronounced x-height and curves that leave their loops unfinished, and that contrast between a tidy display line and a looser, contemporary body is the pair's best trait.
gen-dafont-stentiga-gf-kufam: Stentiga is the refined one, tracked out wide with crossbars as thick as its stems. Kufam does the steady work beneath, a sans-serif with one track width like a neon tube and bodies that dominate the line while ascenders hardly show.
gen-dafont-stentiga-gf-lexend: Wide, polished and a bit indulgent, Stentiga sets the tone with generous spacing. Lexend carries on in a plain sans, its outsized lowercase and open jaws on every curve making a long page feel unhurried and approachable.
gen-dafont-stentiga-gf-lexend-deca: Lexend Deca draws a plain, unshaded line with big lowercase and small-looking capitals, and its terminals stop short of curling back in. Stentiga overhead keeps its luxurious, spread-out spacing, so give the plain sans the room.
gen-dafont-stentiga-gf-liter: Liter reads with no stroke contrast at all, its lowercase standing tall and its round forms wide-mouthed. Stentiga adds the refined, luxurious spacing on top, and that stretch between a display heading and a plain sans is what makes the pair.
gen-dafont-stentiga-gf-mada: Stentiga keeps a single constant stroke width throughout. Mada, a plain sans with a towering midzone and curves that refuse to close, gives it an approachable, modern partner, and the gap in their moods is the pair's best quality.
gen-dafont-stentiga-gf-martel-sans: Stentiga spreads its refined letters wide and keeps the same line width in curves and straights alike, which is what a display face does best. Martel Sans, a plain sans, simply works the text, with a high mean line and open curves.
gen-dafont-stentiga-gf-matangi: Hushed, spaced-out luxury comes from Stentiga, with crossbars as heavy as its stems. Matangi follows in sans-serif, strokes like twine pressed flat and a hefty lowercase, so a longer page of text feels sturdy and modern.
